question: Before any future SDRP-style capacity claim that pretends to cover 5 heuristic classes, should Stage-A-12 (or its successor) be expanded or replaced so salt-bridge and hydrophobe-contact labels actually occur?

fact_locked.implication: No training budget, architecture change, or metric fix on this corpus can ever test whether the model learns salt/hydrophobe — that is corpus composition, not a model problem.

A_keep_stage_a_12_narrow_claim.do: Keep folds_frozen / Stage-A-12 for harness cards; every SDRP capacity prereg must state effective_classes={0,1,4} and forbid 5-class language.
A_keep_stage_a_12_narrow_claim.pros: No new data work; honest scope; instrumentation queue unblocked.
A_keep_stage_a_12_narrow_claim.cons: Never tests salt/hydrophobe on this line.

B_expand_manifest_for_contact_types.cost_class: expensive — not a peer alternative to A/C in cost, even though peer in scope
B_expand_manifest_for_contact_types.do: Design (not run) a successor manifest that includes structures where sdrp_heuristic_from_edges yields nonzero class 2 and/or 3 counts; freeze new folds only after reachability + class-coverage table.
B_expand_manifest_for_contact_types.pros: Makes a future 5-class (or 4-class with salt/hydrophobe) claim possible.
B_expand_manifest_for_contact_types.cons: New data/governance work; must not silently replace Stage-A-12 mid-instrumentation.

cost_asymmetry.why_not_peer_to_A_or_C: B is the only option that requires new data acquisition plus re-verification, on every added structure, of what Stage-A-12 already established: sequence-identity thresholds, wrap-threshold calibration, and R0–R5 graph construction. That is a larger lift than A (claim narrowing) or C (target change on the existing corpus).
required_if_chosen: Per-new-structure class-coverage table (nonzero salt and/or hydrophobe counts)
Reachability re-derivation for any new capacity bars (train + held-out) — train ceilings do not transfer
Re-check wrap-threshold / R0–R5 construction invariants on additions before folds_frozen successor seal
Separate sealed prereg — does not block logger-align / spine-rel / B2

B_expand_manifest_for_contact_types.gate: Separate sealed prereg; does not block logger-align / spine-rel / B2.

C_change_target_not_corpus.cost_class: cheap-to-moderate (design + new bars on existing corpus; no new PDB acquisition)
C_change_target_not_corpus.do: Drop SDRP argmax heuristic for capacity claims; use a target that is present and less majority-dominated on Stage-A-12 (or non-leaking biology target on pool).
C_change_target_not_corpus.pros: Avoids expanding corpus to chase empty classes.
C_change_target_not_corpus.cons: Different scientific question; already partially the trunk path (claim-bearing hyp biology).

cost_note: A/B/C are peer alternatives in *scope* (what claim becomes possible). They are not peer alternatives in *cost*. Prefer A or C unless the scientific need specifically requires salt/hydrophobe coverage — then budget B as its own data+governance card, not a table row next to A.
